name: Adriano Santos
action: Adriano sets the wrench down on the workbench, presses his thumb against the ringing spot below his ear, and picks up the phone. He turns his right side toward the speaker, bringing it close, and speaks a little too loud in that flat, unhurried voice: "Marina. Yeah, I know. Three weeks. I've been on this snare—turquoise wrap, the lug on the fourth side is being a pain. I'm not ignoring you. It's just the work." He pauses, running a hand over the shell, then adds: "Tell Mama I'll come. I'll finish this wrap and then I'll come. Later, not at the start—I don't want to get there while she's still putting things in the oven. But I'll be there for the meal. Don't let them save me a chair next to the stereo this time."
reason: Adriano felt irritation when the phone buzz cut into his concentration on the snare's stubborn turquoise lug, but seeing Marina's name brought guilt over missing three Sundays and memories of the last lunch when he smiled at a joke he reconstructed wrong. Her persistent efforts—like the cake she held up so he could read her lips—made him feel he couldn't let it ring out a fourth time. He recognized his garage as his own quiet corner, like his father's backyard with a cigarette, yet decided the drum could wait. That inner conflict—between his need to finish the work and his sense of obligation—led him to answer, speak too loudly in his flat way, and commit to coming later but not at the start, asking not to sit near the stereo because of his hearing difficulties.
